verbalization: L-carvenyl acetate is proposed to interact with HaCaT cells through a mechanism involving the chloramphenicol acetyltransferase enzyme. This enzyme is a well-characterized target of the compound (2R,4aS,6bR,12aS)-2,10,14b-trihydroxy-4a,6a,6b,9,9,12a-hexamethyl-13-oxo-1,3,4,5,6,6a,7,8,8a,10,11,12-dodecahydropicene-2-carboxylic acid, which is a known substrate of chloramphenicol acetyltransferase. The interaction between L-carvenyl acetate and this enzyme suggests a potential regulatory role in HaCaT cell function, as the enzyme is involved in the metabolism of antibiotics and may influence cellular processes such as proliferation or differentiation. The evidence supports a direct, functional link between L-carvenyl acetate and HaCaT, mediated through this enzymatic pathway.
